claim: Transcriptional recovery after ionizing radiation occurs in a manner independent of the HIRA histone chaperone.
source: In contrast to the situation following UV damage, we found that transcriptional recovery after ionizing radiation (IR) occurs in a manner independent of the HIRA histone chaperone.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, and Figure 1A shows experimental data demonstrating no effect of HIRA depletion on transcriptional recovery after IR.

claim: Most of the loss of nascent transcripts occurring after IR is due to inhibition of transcriptional initiation of the highly transcribed histone genes and the rDNA.
source: Specifically, most of the loss of nascent transcripts occurring after IR is due to inhibition of transcriptional initiation of the highly transcribed histone genes and the rDNA.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, and it is supported by sequencing data shown in Figures 3B, 4A, 4D, 4E, and 4F showing reduced rDNA and histone gene transcripts.

claim: Depletion of HIRA had no effect on transcriptional inhibition nor recovery after IR.
source: We found that shRNA depletion of HIRA (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) had no effect on transcriptional inhibition nor recovery after IR (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 1A which shows quantitative data comparing scramble shRNA and shHIRA conditions.

claim: Depletion of transcripts encoded from both H3.3 genes had no effect on transcriptional inhibition or transcriptional recovery after IR.
source: In agreement, depletion of transcripts encoded from both H3.3 genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) had no effect on transcriptional inhibition or transcriptional recovery after IR (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 1B showing experimental data with siRNA against H3.3 genes.

claim: The requirement for HIRA for transcriptional recovery differs following IR and UV exposure.
source: As such, the requirement for HIRA for transcriptional recovery differs following IR and UV exposure, suggesting differences in the mechanism of these processes.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the experimental data showing HIRA independence after IR, contrasted with cited literature showing HIRA dependence after UV.

claim: A reduction in bulk nascent transcripts was apparent 30 min after exposure to 10 Gray ionizing radiation.
source: A reduction in bulk nascent transcripts was apparent 30 min after exposure to 10 Gray ionizing radiation (IR), and the transcriptional recovery was already occurring 2 hr after irradiation (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1A showing EU incorporation data at different time points after IR.

claim: Transcriptional recovery was already occurring 2 hr after irradiation.
source: A reduction in bulk nascent transcripts was apparent 30 min after exposure to 10 Gray ionizing radiation (IR), and the transcriptional recovery was already occurring 2 hr after irradiation (Figure 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1A showing EU incorporation data at 2 hours post-IR.

claim: The DNA damage signal was greatly reduced at the same time point after IR where transcriptional recovery occurred.
source: Co-immunofluorescence with γH2AX showed that the DNA damage signal was greatly reduced at the same time point after IR where transcriptional recovery occurred (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), consistent with transcriptional recovery occurring after DSB repair.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing γH2AX staining data.

claim: Transcriptional recovery occurs after DSB repair.
source: Co-immunofluorescence with γH2AX showed that the DNA damage signal was greatly reduced at the same time point after IR where transcriptional recovery occurred (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), consistent with transcriptional recovery occurring after DSB repair.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the temporal correlation between reduced γH2AX signal and transcriptional recovery.

claim: The EU signal had 2 peaks corresponding to different cell cycle phases.
source: The EU signal had 2 peaks (Figure 2A) and we asked whether this reflects cell cycle differences in the cells with higher and lower EU incorporation into the nascent transcripts.
evidence: The text explicitly describes this observation and references Figure 2A showing flow cytometry data with two EU peaks.

claim: The peak with less EU was from the G1 phase cells, while the peak with more EU was derived from S and G2 phase cells.
source: It was apparent that the peak with less EU was from the G1 phase cells, while the peak with more EU was derived from S and G2 phase cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 2B showing cell cycle analysis correlated with EU incorporation.

claim: The transcriptional inhibition after irradiation was clearly detectable by flow cytometry as early as 15 min after IR.
source: The transcriptional inhibition after irradiation was clearly detectable by flow cytometry as early as 15 min after IR, while transcriptional recovery was complete by 4 hr after IR (Figure 2D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 2D showing time course data.

claim: Transcriptional recovery was complete by 4 hr after IR.
source: The transcriptional inhibition after irradiation was clearly detectable by flow cytometry as early as 15 min after IR, while transcriptional recovery was complete by 4 hr after IR (Figure 2D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 2D showing time course data.

claim: The extent of transcriptional repression was similar regardless of whether the IR dose was 2, 5, or 10 Gray.
source: Also, the extent of transcriptional repression was similar regardless of whether the IR dose was 2, 5, or 10 Gray (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing dose-response data.

claim: The reduction of nascent transcripts after IR is a programmed/signaling response rather than due to proximity of the genes to the DSB.
source: This is consistent with the possibility that the reduction of nascent transcripts after IR is a programmed/signaling response rather than due to proximity of the genes to the DSB, which would have led to a dose-response.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the dose-independence data, representing a logical inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The total read count of nascent transcripts declined after IR.
source: We observed that the total read count of nascent transcripts declined after IR (Figure 3B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3B showing sequencing read count data.

claim: The decline in bulk transcripts after IR was mostly due to a significant decline in rDNA transcripts.
source: Most of the read counts were due to rDNA transcripts, and the decline in bulk transcripts after IR was mostly due to a significant decline in rDNA transcripts (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A showing rDNA transcript data.

claim: The total read count from the protein-coding transcripts significantly increased after IR.
source: By contrast, the total read count from the protein-coding transcripts significantly increased after IR (Figure 3B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3B showing protein-coding transcript data.

claim: The transcripts of 3026 protein-coding genes increased after IR.
source: Analysis of the protein-coding transcripts showed that the transcripts of 3026 and 1388 protein-coding genes increased and decreased after IR, respectively (Figure 3C and D, Supp. File 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 3C and D showing differential expression analysis.

claim: The transcripts of 1388 protein-coding genes decreased after IR.
source: Analysis of the protein-coding transcripts showed that the transcripts of 3026 and 1388 protein-coding genes increased and decreased after IR, respectively (Figure 3C and D, Supp. File 1).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 3C and D showing differential expression analysis.

claim: rDNA transcripts of 28 S and 18 S were significantly downregulated after IR.
source: Consistently, we found rDNA transcripts of 28 S and 18 S were significantly downregulated after IR; while the p53-regulated gene Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 (Cdkn1a/p21) was highly induced (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 3—figure supplement 3 showing RT-PCR validation data.

claim: The p53-regulated gene Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 (Cdkn1a/p21) was highly induced after IR.
source: Consistently, we found rDNA transcripts of 28 S and 18 S were significantly downregulated after IR; while the p53-regulated gene Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1 (Cdkn1a/p21) was highly induced (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 3—figure supplement 3 showing RT-PCR validation data.

claim: The intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to DNA damage was upregulated significantly after IR.
source: For example, the intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to DNA damage (GO:0008630), type 2 response (GO:0042092), and cytokine-mediated signaling pathway (GO:0019221) were up regulated significantly.
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from gene ontology analysis of upregulated genes.

claim: Type 2 response pathway was upregulated significantly after IR.
source: For example, the intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to DNA damage (GO:0008630), type 2 response (GO:0042092), and cytokine-mediated signaling pathway (GO:0019221) were up regulated significantly.
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from gene ontology analysis of upregulated genes.

claim: Cytokine-mediated signaling pathway was upregulated significantly after IR.
source: For example, the intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in response to DNA damage (GO:0008630), type 2 response (GO:0042092), and cytokine-mediated signaling pathway (GO:0019221) were up regulated significantly.
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from gene ontology analysis of upregulated genes.

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines are rapidly activated after irradiation in various cell types.
source: Pro-inflammatory cytokines are the major components of immediate early gene programs, being rapidly activated after irradiation in various cell types (Schaue et al., 2012) ultimately leading to radiation-induced fibrosis in cancer patients following radiation therapy (Kim et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2023).
evidence: The text explicitly states this claim and cites published literature (Schaue et al., 2012).

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines ultimately lead to radiation-induced fibrosis in cancer patients following radiation therapy.
source: Pro-inflammatory cytokines are the major components of immediate early gene programs, being rapidly activated after irradiation in various cell types (Schaue et al., 2012) ultimately leading to radiation-induced fibrosis in cancer patients following radiation therapy (Kim et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2023).
evidence: The text explicitly states this claim and cites published literature (Kim et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2023).

claim: Chromatin silencing genes were downregulated significantly after IR.
source: For example, chromatin silencing (GO:0006342), DNA packaging (GO:0006323), and nucleosome assembly (GO:0006334) genes were down regulated significantly.
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from gene ontology analysis of downregulated genes.

claim: DNA packaging genes were downregulated significantly after IR.
source: For example, chromatin silencing (GO:0006342), DNA packaging (GO:0006323), and nucleosome assembly (GO:0006334) genes were down regulated significantly.
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from gene ontology analysis of downregulated genes.

claim: Nucleosome assembly genes were downregulated significantly after IR.
source: For example, chromatin silencing (GO:0006342), DNA packaging (GO:0006323), and nucleosome assembly (GO:0006334) genes were down regulated significantly.
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from gene ontology analysis of downregulated genes.

claim: Read number from differentially expressed genes became significantly greater after IR.
source: We found read number from these DEGs became significantly greater after IR (Figure 4A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4A showing read count data for DEGs.

claim: The number of reads derived from the mostly highly expressed protein-coding DEGs became significantly smaller after IR.
source: We sorted the protein-coding DEGs by average expression level of each gene in all four samples: two replicate samples before IR and two replicates after IR. The number of reads derived from the mostly highly expressed protein-coding DEGs became significantly smaller after IR (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 4A and B showing expression data for highly expressed genes.

claim: The length of the nascent transcripts was equivalent regardless of whether their transcription was repressed, activated, or not changed after IR.
source: However, this was not the case because the length of the nascent transcripts was equivalent regardless of whether their transcription was repressed, activated, or not changed after IR (Figure 4C).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4C showing gene length analysis.

claim: The repressed genes of the top 100 high-expression DEGs tended to be shorter.
source: Intriguingly, we found that the repressed genes of the top 100 high-expression DEGs tended to be shorter (Figure 4C).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4C showing gene length analysis for highly expressed genes.

claim: Most changes in gene expression after IR tended to occur for the genes that were activated after IR.
source: Next, we inspected the expression level of individual protein-coding genes and confirmed that most changes in gene expression after IR tended to occur for the genes that were activated after IR, while many of the genes that had a high-expression level were repressed after IR, for example, the histone encoding genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4D showing individual gene expression data.

claim: Many of the genes that had a high-expression level were repressed after IR, for example, the histone encoding genes.
source: Next, we inspected the expression level of individual protein-coding genes and confirmed that most changes in gene expression after IR tended to occur for the genes that were activated after IR, while many of the genes that had a high-expression level were repressed after IR, for example, the histone encoding genes (Figure 4D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4D showing histone gene expression data.

claim: The vast majority of the histone genes showed reduced transcription after IR.
source: Strikingly, we found that the vast majority of the histone genes showed reduced transcription after IR (Figure 4E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), and was validated by RT-PCR analysis (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 4E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 3 showing histone gene expression data.

claim: The decrease of transcripts mainly occurred in the gene body of repressed protein-coding genes with similar intensity at both the 3' and 5' ends of the gene body.
source: We found that the decrease of transcripts mainly occurred in the gene body of these genes with similar intensity at both the 3' and 5' ends of the gene body, which indicates transcriptional repression after IR occurred at the initiation stage of transcription (Figure 4F).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 4F showing read distribution across gene bodies.

claim: Transcriptional repression after IR occurred at the initiation stage of transcription.
source: We found that the decrease of transcripts mainly occurred in the gene body of these genes with similar intensity at both the 3' and 5' ends of the gene body, which indicates transcriptional repression after IR occurred at the initiation stage of transcription (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation of uniform reduction across gene bodies, representing an inference from the data.

claim: The bulk reduction in nascent transcripts after IR is mainly due to reduced transcriptional initiation of the rDNA and histone genes.
source: Therefore, these data indicate that the bulk reduction in nascent transcripts after IR is mainly due to reduced transcriptional initiation of the rDNA and histone genes.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion synthesizing multiple observations from the sequencing data.

claim: gRNAs against ATM were enriched in the high EU cells.
source: We found that gRNAs against ATM were enriched in the high EU cells, consistent with the fact that transcriptional inhibition of a gene after induction of a DSB requires ATM signaling (Shanbhag et al., 2010).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from the CRISPR screen and cites supporting literature.

claim: Transcriptional inhibition of a gene after induction of a DSB requires ATM signaling.
source: We found that gRNAs against ATM were enriched in the high EU cells, consistent with the fact that transcriptional inhibition of a gene after induction of a DSB requires ATM signaling (Shanbhag et al., 2010).
evidence: The text explicitly states this as an established fact and cites published literature (Shanbhag et al., 2010).

claim: gRNAs against most of the machinery that mediates neddylation were enriched in the high EU cells.
source: Other top hits included most of the machinery that mediates neddylation, the post-translational covalent addition of NEDD8, a small ubiquitin-like peptide, onto other proteins (Rabut and Peter, 2008).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding from the CRISPR screen and cites literature defining neddylation.

claim: gRNAs against the gene encoding the neddylation substrate CUL4B were enriched in the high EU cells.
source: We also uncovered gRNAs against the gene encoding the neddylation substrate CUL4B enriched in the high EC cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 5B showing screen results.

claim: Neddylation may have a novel role in transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: These data suggested that neddylation may have a novel role in transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the CRISPR screen results.

claim: Inhibition of ATM greatly reduces transcriptional inhibition 30 min after IR in Abl pre-B cells.
source: We validated the role of ATM in bulk transcriptional inhibition after IR with the ATM inhibitor Ku55933 (Figure 5C).
evidence: The text explicitly states this validation and references Figure 5C showing experimental data with ATM inhibitor.

claim: Depletion of NAE1 greatly reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: To validate a role for neddylation in transcriptional shut off after IR, we depleted NAE1 with a gRNA to Nae1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2) and showed that depletion of NAE1 also greatly reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 5D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 5D showing experimental data with NAE1 depletion.

claim: A 16 hr treatment with the neddylation inhibitor MLN4924 greatly reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Similarly, a 16 hr treatment with the neddylation inhibitor MLN4924 also greatly reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 5E).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 5E showing experimental data with MLN4924 treatment.

claim: Transcriptional inhibition in U2OS cells was significantly reduced upon inhibition of neddylation.
source: To ensure that the role of neddylation in transcriptional inhibition after IR is not unique to the murine Abl pre-B cells, we found that transcriptional inhibition, detected by fluorescence microscopy, in U2OS cells was significantly reduced upon inhibition of neddylation (Figure 5F).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 5F showing experimental data in U2OS cells.

claim: Neddylation is required for efficient transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: As such, these data suggest that neddylation is required for efficient transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the experimental data showing effects of neddylation inhibition.

claim: There was not a significantly higher proportion of neddylated CUL4A or CUL4B in U2OS cells after IR compared to the level of unneddylated CUL4A.
source: We found that when compared to the level of unneddylated CUL4A there was not a significantly higher proportion of neddylated CUL4A or CUL4B in U2OS cells after IR (Figure 6A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 6A showing western blot data.

claim: Loss of CUL4A had no effect on transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Loss of CUL4A had no effect on transcriptional inhibition after IR, while loss of CUL4B partially reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 6B showing experimental data with CUL4A depletion.

claim: Loss of CUL4B partially reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Loss of CUL4A had no effect on transcriptional inhibition after IR, while loss of CUL4B partially reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 6B showing experimental data with CUL4B depletion.

claim: Additional transient bulk gRNA transfection-mediated depletion of CUL4A from cells lacking CUL4B did not further increase the block of transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Additional transient bulk gRNA transfection-mediated depletion of CUL4A from cells lacking CUL4B (depletion of both CUL4A and CUL4B is lethal) did not further increase the block of transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 6—figure supplement 1B showing experimental data with double depletion.

claim: CUL4B but not CUL4A contributes to transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: As such, these data indicate that CUL4B but not CUL4A contributes to transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the differential effects of CUL4A and CUL4B depletion.

claim: Neddylation of CUL4A/CUL4B regulates cell cycle progression.
source: Given that neddylation of CUL4A/CUL4B regulates cell cycle progression (Hannah and Zhou, 2015), and we saw changes in the distribution of the cell cycle phases upon CUL4A/CUL4B depletion and upon blocking neddylation as indicated by the change in relative heights of the EU low (G1) and EU high (S/G2) peaks (Figures 5D, E, 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C), we wondered if cell cycle arrest may be influencing transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: The text explicitly states this as an established fact and cites published literature (Hannah and Zhou, 2015).

claim: Short treatment (1-3 hr) with neddylation inhibitor effectively inhibited neddylation.
source: Accordingly, we inhibited neddylation for 1–3 hr in Abl pre-B cells, which effectively inhibited neddylation (Figure 6C), and tested the effect on transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 6C showing western blot data.

claim: Transcriptional inhibition after IR occurred even upon neddylation inhibition treatment for 1–3 hr.
source: Strikingly, we observed transcriptional inhibition after IR even upon neddylation inhibition treatment for 1–3 hr (Figure 6D), indicating that neddylation is not required for transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 6D showing EU incorporation data.

claim: Neddylation is not required for transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Strikingly, we observed transcriptional inhibition after IR even upon neddylation inhibition treatment for 1–3 hr (Figure 6D), indicating that neddylation is not required for transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that short-term neddylation inhibition does not prevent transcriptional inhibition.

claim: The length of time required for treatment with the neddylation inhibition to block transcriptional inhibition after IR caused arrest of the cell cycle in G2 phase.
source: We also observed that the length of time required for treatment with the neddylation inhibition to block transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 5E) caused arrest of the cell cycle in G2 phase (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing cell cycle analysis data.

claim: The cell cycle arrest caused by persistent loss of neddylation may prevent transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Therefore, these data indicate that neddylation per se is not required for transcriptional inhibition after IR. They also raise the possibility that the cell cycle arrest caused by persistent loss of neddylation may prevent transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the correlation between neddylation inhibition duration, cell cycle arrest, and transcriptional inhibition.

claim: Prolonged neddylation inhibition led to accumulation of cells with a 4 N DNA content and greatly reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Prolonged neddylation inhibition led to accumulation of cells with a 4 N DNA content and greatly reduced transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 7A, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7A and Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing flow cytometry data.

claim: CDK1 inhibition caused accumulation of cells with a 4 N DNA content and no transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: We also saw accumulation of cells with a 4 N DNA content and no transcriptional inhibition after IR upon CDK1 inhibition (Figure 7B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2 showing flow cytometry data.

claim: Treatment with 0.1% FBS led to arrest in G1 phase and prevented transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: To determine whether this effect was unique to cells arrested with a 4 N DNA content or was shared with conditions that cause arrest in G1 phase, we treated cells with 10% or 0.1% FBS, where the later lead to arrest in G1 phase (due to serum depletion) and prevented transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 7C).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7C showing flow cytometry data.

claim: The level of bulk nascent transcripts in cells arrested in G1 by serum depletion is still far higher than cells lacking EU.
source: It is relevant to point out that the level of bulk nascent transcripts in cells arrested in G1 by serum depletion is still far higher than cells lacking EU (Figure 7C), suggesting that the limited transcriptional inhibition after IR in G1 arrested cells is not just because there is only minimal transcription occurring.
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7C showing EU incorporation data.

claim: Two CDK4/6 inhibitors, Ribociclib and Palbociclib, that lead to G1 arrest also prevented transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: In agreement, two CDK4/6 inhibitors, Ribociclib and Palbociclib, that lead to G1 arrest also prevented transcriptional inhibition after IR (Figure 7D and E).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7D and E showing flow cytometry data.

claim: Multiple different treatments that lead to cell cycle arrest in G1 or G2 per se prevent transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: Intriguingly, these data indicate that multiple different treatments that lead to cell cycle arrest in G1 or G2 per se prevent transcriptional inhibition after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion synthesizing observations from multiple cell cycle arrest experiments.

claim: The percentage of cells with TOPBP1-eGFP localizing to nucleolar caps after IR was markedly reduced upon MLN4924 and RO-3306 treatment.
source: However, the percentage of cells with TOPBP1-eGFP localizing to nucleolar caps after IR was markedly reduced upon MLN4924 and RO-3306 treatment (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 7F and G showing microscopy and quantification data.

claim: Arrested cells fail to repress rDNA expression after global DNA damage, as a consequence of compromised ATM-dependent localization of TOPB1 to nucleolar caps.
source: These results are consistent with arrested cells failing to repress rDNA expression after global DNA damage, as a consequence of compromised ATM-dependent localization of TOPB1 to nucleolar caps.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the TOPBP1 localization data, representing an inference from the experimental observations.

claim: More protein-coding genes are induced than inhibited after IR.
source: We find that while the bulk abundance of nascent transcripts is rapidly reduced after IR, more protein-coding genes are induced than inhibited after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a summary finding in the Discussion section, synthesizing the sequencing data.

claim: The reduction in bulk nascent transcript levels that occurs after IR is due to reduced transcriptional initiation of a subset of genes that are the most highly expressed in the cell – the rDNA and histone encoding genes.
source: Instead, the reduction in bulk nascent transcript levels that occurs after IR is due to reduced transcriptional initiation of a subset of genes that are the most highly expressed in the cell – the rDNA and histone encoding genes.
evidence: This is stated as a summary finding in the Discussion section, synthesizing the sequencing data.

claim: Bulk transcriptional inhibition after IR did not occur in cells arrested in G1 or G2 phases of the cell cycle.
source: Notably, bulk transcriptional inhibition after IR did not occur in cells arrested in G1 or G2 phases of the cell cycle indicating that cells need to be cycling for IR to rapidly inhibit bulk transcription.
evidence: This is stated as a summary finding in the Discussion section, synthesizing the cell cycle arrest experiments.

claim: Cells need to be cycling for IR to rapidly inhibit bulk transcription.
source: Notably, bulk transcriptional inhibition after IR did not occur in cells arrested in G1 or G2 phases of the cell cycle indicating that cells need to be cycling for IR to rapidly inhibit bulk transcription.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that cell cycle arrest prevents transcriptional inhibition.

claim: The reduced bulk abundance of nascent transcripts after IR may occur in trans as a programmed event.
source: The length-independent and dose-independent reduction in bulk abundance of nascent transcript after IR (Figure 4C, Figure 2D) suggests that the reduced bulk abundance of nascent transcripts after IR may occur in trans as a programmed event.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the length-independence and dose-independence observations.

claim: The genome-wide transcriptional response to DSBs after IR cannot be extrapolated from single gene studies.
source: This is in contrast to studies that have found transcriptional inhibition in cis of a gene immediately adjacent to an endonuclease-induced DSB. Our work indicates that the genome-wide transcriptional response to DSBs after IR cannot be extrapolated from single gene studies.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the differences between their genome-wide findings and previous single-gene studies.

claim: Analysis of nascent transcripts at early times after irradiation revealed a different transcriptional response compared to changes in total mRNAs after irradiation.
source: Analysis of nascent transcripts at early times after irradiation revealed a different transcriptional response compared to changes in total mRNAs after irradiation (Lieberman et al., 2017).
evidence: The text explicitly states this comparison and cites published literature (Lieberman et al., 2017).

claim: The bulk changes in nascent transcripts occurred in a dose-independent manner.
source: By contrast, the bulk changes in nascent transcripts occurred in a dose-independent manner (Figure 2D).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 2D showing dose-response data.

claim: The reduction of bulk nascent transcript levels after IR was dependent on ATM.
source: Reminiscent of the ATM dependence on the changes in mRNA levels after IR (Artuso et al., 1995), the reduction in bulk nascent transcript levels after IR was also dependent on ATM (Figure 5C).
evidence: The text explicitly states this finding and references Figure 5C showing experimental data with ATM inhibitor.

claim: Most of the reduction in bulk nascent transcript levels was due mainly to the rRNA.
source: This is likely because most of the reduction in bulk nascent transcript level that we were detecting after IR was due mainly to reduced transcript abundance from the rDNA, rather than Pol II transcripts (Figure 3B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references Figure 3B showing sequencing data.

claim: ATM is required for rDNA transcriptional inhibition after IR.
source: We did find ATM in the screen (Figure 5B and C), and this is consistent with the fact that ATM is required for rDNA transcriptional inhibition after IR (Kruhlak et al., 2007).
evidence: The text explicitly states this as an established fact and cites published literature (Kruhlak et al., 2007).

claim: Neddylation is not directly involved in transcriptional inhibition after IR, but neddylation promotes cell cycle progression.
source: These results lead us to speculate that neddylation is not directly involved in transcriptional inhibition after IR, but that neddylation promotes cell cycle progression, and that it is the cell cycle arrest occurring upon neddylation inhibition that prevents the bulk reduction of nascent transcript levels after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the differential effects of short-term versus long-term neddylation inhibition.

claim: It is the cell cycle arrest occurring upon neddylation inhibition that prevents the bulk reduction of nascent transcript levels after IR.
source: These results lead us to speculate that neddylation is not directly involved in transcriptional inhibition after IR, but that neddylation promotes cell cycle progression, and that it is the cell cycle arrest occurring upon neddylation inhibition that prevents the bulk reduction of nascent transcript levels after IR.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the correlation between cell cycle arrest and loss of transcriptional inhibition.

claim: Cell cycle arrest in G1 or G2 phases of the cell cycle prevents transcriptional repression of rDNA and histone genes after IR.
source: Why would cell cycle arrest in G1 or G2 phases of the cell cycle prevent transcriptional repression of rDNA and histone genes after IR?
evidence: This is stated as a question introducing discussion of the mechanism, implicitly asserting the phenomenon.

claim: Transcription of rDNA is known to be reduced in non-cycling cells when total transcript levels were measured.
source: Transcription of rDNA is known to be reduced in non-cycling cells when total transcript levels were measured (Moss and Stefanovsky, 1995; O'Mahony et al., 1992) while transcription of histone genes requires ongoing DNA replication (Sittman et al., 1983).
evidence: The text explicitly states this as established knowledge and cites published literature (Moss and Stefanovsky, 1995; O'Mahony et al., 1992).

claim: Transcription of histone genes requires ongoing DNA replication.
source: Transcription of rDNA is known to be reduced in non-cycling cells when total transcript levels were measured (Moss and Stefanovsky, 1995; O'Mahony et al., 1992) while transcription of histone genes requires ongoing DNA replication (Sittman et al., 1983).
evidence: The text explicitly states this as established knowledge and cites published literature (Sittman et al., 1983).

claim: The total level of bulk nascent transcripts during G2 arrest before IR were equivalent to, or more than, the level of bulk nascent transcripts before cell cycle arrest.
source: However, we found that the total level of bulk nascent transcripts during G2 arrest before IR were equivalent to, or more than, the level of bulk nascent transcripts before cell cycle arrest (compare gray (no arrest) to black lines (cell cycle arrest) in Figures 5C–E–7A and B) which suggest that the levels of rDNA transcripts may not be reduced during G2 arrest in our experiments given that most of the nascent transcripts are from the rDNA in the conditions of our experiments (Figure 7B).
evidence: The text explicitly states this observation and references multiple figures showing EU incorporation data.

claim: A factor that is required for transcriptional inhibition of the rDNA after IR may be absent or inactive in arrested cells.
source: It is also possible that a factor that is required for transcriptional inhibition of the rDNA after IR is absent or inactive in arrested cells.

claim: In vertebrate cells, the DNA damage response is mediated through activation of three PI3-like kinases: ATM, ATR, and DNA-PK.
source: In vertebrate cells, the DNA damage response is mediated through activation of three PI3-like kinases: ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM), Ataxia telangiectasia and Rad3-related (ATR), and DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PK) (Blackford and Jackson, 2017), which coordinates DNA repair and the DNA damage cell cycle checkpoint which arrests cells until DSBs are repaired.
evidence: The text explicitly states this as established knowledge and cites published literature (Blackford and Jackson, 2017).
